summary: Long-run sector strategy covering productivity, water-use efficiency, land expansion and rural livelihoods. AgriTech4Egypt and the 2026 food-security pillars are aligned with it.
title: Sustainable Agricultural Development Strategy 2030

summary: About 2.2 million feddans west of the Delta, irrigated with treated drainage water from El Hammam. About LE800bn (~$15bn) invested in land, silos, industrial zones and roads.
title: New Delta (Future of Egypt) land reclamation project

summary: Revived desert reclamation in Aswan, targeting wheat and dates, with private and state farms, silos and pumped irrigation.
title: Toshka agricultural project (South Valley)

summary: Expand reclaimed land by 3.5 million feddans, raise yields with technology, close the protein gap, grow exports, and digitize farmer data and AI.
title: Five-pillar food security strategy

summary: Digital smart card that links registered farmers to subsidized fertilizer and other services.
title: Farmer's Card (Kart El Fallah) e-payment for fertilizer

summary: Supports 105 startups (350+ innovators) through challenges, mentoring, validation and pilots with ARC and ASRT.
title: AgriTech4Egypt (Egypt-Italy)

summary: Successor to Plan Maroc Vert: human-capital focus, rural middle class, 1m ha drip; 108bn MAD contracted
title: Generation Green 2020-2030

summary: Dams, inter-basin transfers, desalination; funding raised to ~150bn MAD
title: National Programme for Drinking Water Supply and Irrigation (PNAEPI) 2020-2027

summary: Scale seawater desalination for coastal cities and to free conventional water for agriculture
title: Desalination target 1.7bn m3/yr by 2030

summary: Drip conversion subsidised via FDA; ~930,000 ha reached by mid-2026
title: Localized irrigation target: 1m ha by 2030

summary: Predecessor strategy; built export agriculture, aggregation model and FDA subsidies
title: Plan Maroc Vert 2008-2020

summary: Second-generation CAADP investment plan (~12,391bn FCFA) focused on modernization, value addition and resilience.
title: PNIA 2 (Programme National d'Investissement Agricole 2018-2025)

summary: Aligned to the PND 2026-2030. Five axes: food sovereignty, competitiveness, financing, rural land security, climate resilience and sustainability.
title: PNIA 3 (third-generation agricultural investment programme)

summary: Legal basis for customary-to-certified rural land rights. AFOR and the World Bank-backed PRESFOR are accelerating certificates.
title: Rural Land Law (Loi n°98-750) and PRESFOR land-security programme

summary: CCC-administered marketing system that guarantees a farm-gate price of at least 60% of the international price.
title: Cocoa/coffee marketing reform (forward sales, minimum 60% of CIF price)

summary: CNRA's 10-year plan covering climate adaptation, productivity, food safety, genetic resources and faster delivery of innovations to farmers.
title: National Agronomic Research Strategic Plan 2026-2035

summary: Regional agro-industrial clusters (e.g., Agropole Sud, Nord) for processing and market access.
title: Agropoles (agro-industrial poles) programme

summary: Flagship agriculture programme: irrigation rehabilitation, small dams, solar boreholes, Farmer Service Centres, seed systems (e.g., rice-seed independence by 2027), urban farmers' markets and agro-industrial linkages.
title: Feed Ghana Programme

summary: Input subsidy and credit programme (PFJ 2.0 from 2023 shifted to input credit). Replaced by Feed Ghana after the 2025 change of government.
title: Planting for Food and Jobs (PFJ 1.0 and 2.0)

summary: Poultry value-chain programme under Feed Ghana to cut chicken imports. GH¢36.75m in the H1 2026 allotment.
title: Nkoko Nkitinkiti (poultry) Programme

summary: COCOBOD and MoF policy shift toward local bean processing, local bond financing and arrears clearance.
title: Cocoa sector reforms / local processing drive

summary: Funds Farmer Service Centres, fertilizer and seed, irrigation, NAFCO and oil-palm development. MoFA and MoF disagree publicly over releases.
title: 2026 Budget agriculture allocations

summary: Sector policy on productivity, mechanisation, digital agriculture, value chains and climate; anchors NAGS-AP
title: National Agricultural Technology and Innovation Policy (NATIP) 2022-2027

summary: AfDB $200m sector budget support (from Mar 2026, 4 yrs) for inputs and tech; targets 5x wheat, +20% rice
title: National Agricultural Growth Scheme - Agro-Pocket (NAGS-AP), Phase II

summary: AfDB and partners mobilise $2.2bn to extend agro-industrial zones to 24 states (phase 1: 7 states + FCT)
title: Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ) Phase 2

summary: Seven-pillar cooperative reform framework approved in March 2026
title: Renewed Hope Cooperative Reform and Revamp Programme (RH-CRRP 2030)

summary: Digital farmer registry linked to National Identity Number for targeting inputs and digital extension
title: National Farmers Registry (NIN-linked) and e-extension

summary: Vests land in state governors; certificate-of-occupancy system widely seen as limiting farmland titling and collateral
title: Land Use Act

summary: Federal rural land law: registration, leasing and collateralisation of use-rights; central land database
title: Rural Land Administration and Use Proclamation No. 1324/2024

summary: ATI/MoA roadmap: 6 solutions across 22 priority areas; phase 1 (2025-29) foundations, phase 2 scale-up
title: Digital Agriculture Roadmap 2025-2032

summary: ATI-led clustering of smallholders; ~12.3m ha by 2024/25
title: Agricultural Commercialization Clusters / cluster farming

summary: Large-scale dry-season irrigated wheat in lowlands to cut wheat imports
title: Lowland irrigated wheat import-substitution initiative

summary: National development plan with agriculture as a lead growth sector
title: Ten Years Development Plan 2021-2030

status: approved by Council of Ministers; referred to parliament
summary: Legal framework for contract farming to raise productivity and market linkages
title: Contract Farming Proclamation

summary: Ten-year sector plan with nine flagships: farmer incomes, value addition, food resilience, digital and data
title: Agricultural Sector Transformation and Growth Strategy (ASTGS) 2019-2029

summary: Roadmap to grow irrigated area from 664k acres (2021/22) to 1.29m acres by 2027/28 and expand water storage
title: National Irrigation Sector Investment Plan (NISIP)

summary: Subsidised fertiliser (Ksh2,500 per bag) for KIAMIS-registered farmers; 12.5m bags released for the 2026 long rains
title: National Fertilizer Subsidy Programme via KIAMIS e-voucher

summary: Framework to scale agroecological practices, soil health and climate resilience
title: National Agroecology Strategy for Food System Transformation 2024-2033

summary: Ministry delivery plan aligned with the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) value chains
title: MoALD Strategic Plan 2023-2027

summary: Targets rice self-sufficiency through irrigation schemes and mechanisation
title: National Rice Development Strategy 2019-2030

summary: RWF 6.6trn (~US$5.1bn) food-systems and climate-resilience plan; ~44% private financing
title: Fifth Strategic Plan for Agriculture Transformation (PSTA5) 2024-2029

summary: National plan: +50% priority crop output, >6% ag growth, double ag exports to US$1.9bn
title: National Strategy for Transformation (NST2) 2024-2029

summary: Expand irrigated area 85% to 132,961 ha by 2029; marshland irrigation to 42,473 ha
title: Irrigation expansion target to 2029

summary: Halves interest on farm loans; RWF 55bn approved, 30.9bn disbursed via 31 FIs
title: Concessional agricultural lending scheme

summary: Largest ministry increase, mainly for fertiliser subsidies, post-harvest storage, strategic grain reserves
title: FY2026/27 budget: MINAGRI allocation +41.3%

summary: Targets more than 10% agricultural growth by 2030, $5bn+ agri exports, 8.5 million ha irrigated, post-harvest losses cut from 35% to 5%, and agro-processing from 10% to 50%.
title: Agenda 10/30

summary: Youth block farms with irrigation, land allocation, training and start-up support. Anchors the TZS 1.1tn 2026/27 budget.
title: Building a Better Tomorrow (BBT) Youth and Women Initiative

summary: 67,000 subsidized boreholes and pumps, plus 1,000 solar pumps, 146 construction projects and 634 scheme designs.
title: Smallholder Irrigation Borehole Programme (NIRC)

summary: Sector-wide framework covering land and water, productivity, commercialization and coordination. CAADP-aligned.
title: Agricultural Sector Development Programme II (ASDP II)

summary: Long-term national vision with agriculture and agro-industrialization as core pillars.
title: Tanzania Development Vision 2050

summary: About TZS 1.1tn, with a target of 2.1 million tonnes of cash crops (+32%), 235,000 t of avocado and NAESA operational from July 2026.
title: Ministry of Agriculture 2026/27 budget

summary: Social compact of government, business, labour and civil society to grow output, exports, jobs and inclusion across value chains.
title: Agriculture and Agro-processing Master Plan (AAMP)

summary: R3.2bn blended-finance window that combines grants and Land Bank loans for black and emerging producers.
title: Blended Finance Scheme (Department of Agriculture and Land Bank)

summary: Mass FMD vaccination (13.5m+ doses imported), state vaccination where farmers lack means, and biosecurity compliance for trade.
title: FMD control and vaccination strategy

summary: Replaces the 1975 Act and sets out expropriation procedures, including nil compensation in limited cases. Contested in courts and within the GNU.
title: Expropriation Act

summary: Reforms opening rail and ports to private operators, addressing export logistics constraints that matter for agriculture.
title: National Logistics Crisis Committee / Freight Logistics Roadmap

status: Superseded by Malabo (2014) and Kampala (2026-35); the 10% budget target remains a reference point
summary: Created CAADP; pledged at least 10% of national budgets to agriculture and 6% annual agricultural growth. Most countries never consistently hit the 10% target.
title: Maputo Declaration / CAADP launch

status: Expired 2025. In the 4th Biennial Review (2023), no country was on track (benchmark 9.29); the hunger-by-2025 goal was missed by all member states
summary: Seven commitments: recommit to CAADP, 10% spending, end hunger by 2025, halve poverty, triple intra-African agri trade, enhance resilience, mutual accountability through biennial reviews.
title: Malabo Declaration on Accelerated Agricultural Growth and Transformation

status: Adopted 11 Jan 2025 at the Extraordinary AU Summit in Kampala; implementation began 2026 (national agrifood systems investment plans being domesticated)
summary: By 2035: mobilize US$100bn public and private investment, raise agrifood output 45%, halve post-harvest loss, triple intra-African trade in agrifood products and inputs, raise local processing to 35% of agrifood GDP, eradicate PPR by 2030, empower women and youth, strengthen governance.
title: Kampala CAADP Declaration on Building Resilient and Sustainable Agrifood Systems (CAADP Strategy & Action Plan 2026-2035)

status: In force 30 May 2019; trading from 1 Jan 2021. 50 of 54 signatories ratified (Sept 2026). 26 states had gazetted tariff schedules by June 2026. 100% of rules of origin agreed Feb 2026. Guided Trade Initiative (2022) concluded 2025. Phase II protocols (investment, IP, competition, digital trade, women and youth) await ratification
summary: Single market for goods and services across 54 states. Liberalizes 90% of tariff lines, plus protocols on services, investment, digital trade, and a planned industrial policy protocol.
title: Agreement Establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)

status: PAP I (2012-2020): ~409 projects; commitments of US$82bn vs US$67.9bn projected. PAP II (2021-2030): 69 projects, ~US$160.7bn, corridor approach, adopted 2021
summary: Cross-border transport, energy, transboundary water and ICT backbone, with ~US$360bn total infrastructure need projected to 2040. Key for agri corridors and power pools.
title: Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA) - PAP I and PAP II

status: Adopted at the AFSH Summit in Nairobi, 7-9 May 2024; implementation and country roadmaps under way; financing via AfDB-hosted Africa Fertilizer Financing Mechanism
summary: Triple fertilizer use from 18 to 54 kg/ha by 2034; double cereal yields from 1.7 to 3.5 t/ha; put 30% of land under sustainable soil management (from 8.2%); keep nitrogen use efficiency at 60% or above; give 70% of farmers access to advisory services; double agricultural growth to 8%. Endorsed the Soil Initiative for Africa.
title: Nairobi Declaration and Africa Fertilizer & Soil Health (AFSH) Action Plan 2024-2034

status: Active; mid-term implementation; continental data governance frameworks under validation (Dec 2025) toward a Digital Single Market by 2030
summary: Aims at a Digital Single Market by 2030. Pillars include digital infrastructure, skills, digital agriculture, and e-government. Basis for the AU Data Policy Framework.
title: Digital Transformation Strategy for Africa 2020-2030

status: Released 28 July 2022; being domesticated; calls for ratification of the Malabo Convention on cyber security and data protection
summary: Principles for data governance, cross-border data flows, data protection, and value enablers. Builds on the DTS and enables farmer-data sharing and DPI interoperability.
title: AU Data Policy Framework

link: https://au.int/en/agenda2063/overview (could not be opened: fetch blocked; standard AU URL)
status: Active; Second Ten-Year Implementation Plan (2024-2033) under way. Flagships include AfCFTA, PIDA, and the Single African Air Transport Market
summary: 50-year vision. Agriculture modernization, industrialization and integrated infrastructure are core goals; CAADP is the agriculture vehicle.
title: Agenda 2063: The Africa We Want

status: Held Jan 2023; US$72bn mobilized. By May 2024, 6 countries had presidential delivery councils and 12 more were setting them up
summary: Country compacts to scale proven technologies (TAAT): heat-tolerant wheat, maize, rice, soybean, and livestock. Linked to Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones.
title: Dakar 2 Summit: Feed Africa - Food Sovereignty and Resilience
type: AfDB-led heads of state summit + Country Food & Agriculture Delivery Compacts

status: Launched 2024; Dar es Salaam Energy Summit Jan 2025 national compacts. 64m people connected by Oct 2026 (WBG 59m, AfDB 5m+)
summary: Connect 300 million Africans to electricity by 2030 through grid and distributed renewables, utility reform and private capital. Critical for irrigation, cold chain and processing.
title: Mission 300 (World Bank Group & African Development Bank)
type: MDB energy access initiative + national energy compacts

status: Active framework; reinforced by the Niamey Extraordinary Summit on Industrialization (25 Nov 2022)
summary: Seven clusters: industrial policy, production and trade capacity, infrastructure and energy, skills, innovation and R&D, finance, sustainability. Niamey 2022 committed 5-10% of budgets to industry, 10% of public procurement for local firms, SEZs as regional value chain hubs, food and cotton value chains, and an African Industrial Development Index.
title: Accelerated Industrial Development for Africa (AIDA) Plan of Action

status: Adopted Nov 2022; AU Commission developing regional value chain recommendations; AfCFTA mandated to negotiate an Industrial Policy protocol
summary: Commodity-based industrialization via regional value chains (agro-food, cotton apparel, pharma, minerals, automotive), SEZs/industrial parks, local procurement and skills.
title: Niamey Declaration on Industrialization and Economic Diversification

status: Partially implemented. COMESA: 7 of 21 states had domesticated rules by 2018. Regional variety catalogues are operational (COMESA, SADC) and companies list varieties via Seeds2B. ECOWAS/UEMOA/CILSS share a regional catalogue
summary: Mutual recognition of variety release, certification and phytosanitary rules: a variety released in 2 member states can be marketed region-wide, cutting time and cost to market.
title: Regional seed harmonization (ECOWAS 2008 regulation; SADC Harmonized Seed Regulatory System 2008/2013; COMESA COMSHIP 2014)
